question: Is PEMSEA’s CvSU ASEANO Subproject 1 report the public output for CvSU’s listed Imus watershed biophysical-characterization project, and does it provide fish evidence or reusable GIS geometry?

sourceReviews.finding: CvSU lists “Bio-physical Characterization, Vulnerability and Pollution Assessment in Imus River Watershed” under Prof. Noel A. Sedigo, CAFENR, funded by PEMSEA, for November 2020–April 2021. The listing itself provides no report or dataset link.

The official PEMSEA PDF is titled “ASEANO 2020–2021, Subproject 1: Mapping and Characterization of Imus River Watershed Using Geographic Information System and Remote Sensing Technology.” It names N.A. Sedigo among CvSU authors. Its subject, institution, PI, funder and period strongly align with the CvSU listing, so it is a probable related project output, but neither document explicitly cross-references the listing title or says this is the complete project deliverable.

PEMSEA’s March 2023 partnership story says ASEANO technical reports had been turned over to the Cavite Government. It does not enumerate those reports, identify the complete CvSU project deliverable, or mention a fish-tissue study.

describedTopics: DEM-based Imus River watershed delineation and boundary mapping
barangay, population, land-cover and land-use mapping
hydroclimatic context and streamflow at a gauge near Daang Hari Bridge

reportSpecificMeasures.warning: Report-specific watershed measurements only; not a validated fish distribution, river-channel length, or fishing-ground boundary.

fishEvidenceSearch.interpretation: The PDF discusses land use and includes a fishpond land-use class, but the reviewed report provides no fish survey, taxa, sampling sites, vouchers, or fish occurrence table. This conclusion is limited to the report text reviewed.

geometry.decision: Do not digitize, publish, or treat printed PDF maps as a validated Bangwit fishing-area boundary. The report describes DEM-derived work but no reusable vector file was found in the reviewed public materials.

rightsReview.decision: Retain only short attributed bibliographic and scope metadata. Do not reproduce report text, maps, or spatial data in the app without item-specific permission review.

nextAction: Continue independent fish-source research. Keep this probable watershed-mapping component distinct from the full CvSU project listing, the IYRR SORB, and the unnamed Bacoor fish-tissue study. Seek reusable GIS or fish-specific results only through verified public files or a separately authorized source request.
